feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Canada's retaliatory tariffs against the U.S. go into effect, escalating trade war
entry.summary: Canada's retaliatory tariffs against U.S. imports went into effect early Tuesday, escalating the trade war between former close allies.

entry.title: Chrystia Freeland negotiated with Trump. Now she's watching a trade war unfold
entry.summary: Chrystia Freeland understands the U.S.-Canada relationship from her time at the negotiating table. Here's what she sees now.

entry.title: Hurricane Lowell could cause flooding, mudslides in western Hawaii
entry.summary: Hurricane Lowell triggers hurricane warnings on its approach to western Hawaii as a major Category 3 storm.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: Canada's retaliatory tariffs against the U.S. go into effect, Republicans prepare for Trump's unconventional midterm convention, officials say victims in Miami airport crash were inside vehicles.

entry.title: 'All The Presidents' Wars' examines America's war on terror from Bush to Trump
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with journalist Peter Bergen about his latest book, "All The Presidents' Wars," a history of the United States' war on terror across four presidential administrations.

entry.title: Law professor discusses SCOTUS' recent approach on who can sue the president
entry.summary: Who has the right to sue the president? NPR's Leila Fadel asks Georgetown Law professor Stephen Vladeck about the Supreme Court's approach to standing when it comes to the Trump administration.

entry.title: Many Americans have no memory of 9/11. A foundation hopes an artifact can change that
entry.summary: The Tunnels to Towers Foundation is traveling across the U.S. with a 21-foot I-beam from the World Trade Center's South Tower to help educate Americans with no memory of the Sept. 11 attacks.

entry.title: Georgia and South Carolina are working to eradicate an invasive, bee-eating hornet
entry.summary: Georgia and South Carolina are trying to fight off an invasive bee-eating hornet that's been spreading along their coasts.

entry.title: Renovated space at National Civil Rights Museum connects the past and future
entry.summary: A new space at the National Civil Rights Museum in Memphis explores the recent past and future of the movement.

entry.title: Virginia preschoolers embark on their very first day of school
entry.summary: It's the first day of school for millions of students, including preschoolers at Charles City Elementary School, located outside Richmond, Virginia.
